prompt: Our NestJS service is containerized for CI, and right now every single commit triggers a full Docker image rebuild that takes roughly 8 minutes — even a one-line, code-only change reinstalls all npm dependencies from scratch, with nothing served from cache. Here's the current Dockerfile. Diagnose why the layer cache is missing on every build, then optimize the Dockerfile so a code-only commit no longer pays the full dependency-install cost while a genuine dependency change (a lockfile edit) still rebuilds correctly. State the expected wall-clock improvement and describe exactly how you'd verify it.
givenCode:
FROM node:20.11.1-alpine

WORKDIR /app

# Bring in the whole project before installing anything
COPY . .

# Install dependencies against whatever package.json/package-lock.json
# happened to come along in the full source copy above
RUN npm ci --omit=dev

RUN npm run build

EXPOSE 3000

CMD ["node", "dist/main.js"]
